newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SYRACUSE, MIAMI, WISCONSIN WIN BOWL GAMES.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SYRACUSE, MIAMI, WISCONSIN WIN BOWL GAMES.

text.p: Malcolm Thomas rushed for a career-high 201 yards and quarterback Donovan McNabb ran for two touchdowns as Syracuse defeated Houston 30-17 in the Liberty Bowl Friday.

Syracuse (9-3), which had 396 yards rushing on 64 carries, took the lead for good on a two-yard run by fullback Rob Konrad with 9:02 to play in the first half. Thomas carried 24 times for the Orangemen, who won their seventh straight bowl game.
"My job was easy today, the horses up front did all the work," said Thomas.

The Orangemen had debated whether to attend the Liberty Bowl after being bypassed by the Gator Bowl. Gator Bowl officials declined to invite Syracuse to play against North Carolina because the game would have been a rematch of a regular-season game.

"Our motivation for this game was that it allowed our guys a great opportunity to come together one more time," said McNabb. "Coming into the game, we felt that Houston was a great team and presented a real challenge to us."
Antowain Smith ran for a touchdown and caught a pass for another for Houston (7-5).

In the Carquest Bowl at Pro Player Stadium in Miami, safety Tremain Mack scored two touchdowns and Ryan Clement threw for a career-high 274 yards to lead Miami to its first bowl victory in five years, 31-21 over Virginia.

Miami (9-3), which tied Syracuse and Virginia Tech for first place in the Big East, evened its all-time bowl mark at 12-12. The Hurricanes snapped a three-game bowl losing streak, winning for the first time since a 22-0 blanking of Nebraska in the 1991 Orange Bowl.

"This is a crazy feeling," said Miami fifth-year centre K.C. Jones. "I've had nothing but fun and I'm going to miss the guys here. We protected and Ryan threw the ball well. This win will give us momentum going into next year and I hope we compete for the national championship.
"To psyche myself before the game I took the Cavalier media guide and cut out the pictures of the defensive players and ate them."
Clement was 16-of-26 with a pair of interceptions and Tony Gaiter caught three passes for 101 yards.
In the Copper Bowl in Tucson, Arizona, Ron Dayne capped a spectacular freshman year by rushing for 246 yards and three touchdowns to lead Wisconsin to a 38-10 rout of Utah.
Dayne finished with 2,109 yards, breaking the Big Ten single-season record of 2,066 set by Michigan State's Lorenzo White in 1985.
He already had broken NCAA freshman records for rushing yards (1,863) and carries (295) and was coming off a four-touchdown, 399-yard effort at Hawaii in the regular-season finale.

"The coaches and fans have been there for us all year," Dayne said. "I just want to give all my credit to my offensive line. I'm really going to miss my offensive line." Four of the offensive linemen for Wisconsin (8-5) are seniors.

Utah sophomore Chris Fuamatu-Ma'Afala, who averaged 122.8 yards per game in the regular season, had to be carted off in the first quarter with torn ligaments in his left ankle. He had four carries for five yards.
"It affected our offence when he (Fuamatu-Ma'Afala) went out with the injury," said coach Ron McBride of Utah (8-4).
